subject: Acme POC Kickoff - Recap & Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC Kickoff - Recap & Next Steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and suggested next steps so we can get the POC kicked off next week. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent latency across model endpoints during peak trading windows (~250–400ms variance)
- High per-token costs from bursty batch patterns and duplicate prefix prompts
- Need for data isolation and audit logs for regulatory reviews

Goals for the POC:
1) Demonstrate steady tail latency <= 150ms p95 for the 512-token inference scenario
2) Reduce per-token cost by 30% vs current baseline using batching + prefix caching/quantization recommendations
3) Validate audit logging + SSO access controls for compliance review

Proposed POC scope (high level):
- Duration: 4 weeks (pilot environment in Redwood Dedicated)
- Workloads: 2 production prompts + 10 representative eval prompts (we'll use the prompt set attached)
- Success metrics: latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, functional parity on 200 eval prompts
- Owners: Marissa (AE) — commercial & milestones; Rishi (Solutions Engineer) — technical onboarding & runbook; Vanessa (Customer Success) — post-pilot rollout plan

Immediate next steps:
1) Confirm kickoff date (we propose Tue, May 19)
2) Share access: provide a service account email for RBAC + SSO requirements (see access section in attached scope)
3) Exchange prompt/eval CSV (attached) and test dataset redaction notes
4) Sign SOW/POC MOU (I can push DocuSign link once dates confirmed)

Attachments: acme-poc-scope.xlsx (POC MOP), acme-sample-prompt-set.csv

Looking forward — happy to jump on a 30m kickoff to align owners.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme POC Kickoff - Recap & Next Steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and reflects our conversation. A few clarifying questions before we confirm the kickoff: 

1) For the latency target, is the 150ms p95 for cold starts or warm-cache conditions? Our main concern is warm-cache performance during midday spikes.
2) On data isolation — can you confirm whether logs will be stored in our VPC project or in Redwood-managed storage with export hooks? We need to flag this to Security.
3) We have a legal lead who may want to see the MOU; can you please include a high-level statement on data retention and deletion?

Tom and I are available Tue 19th after 11am ET. If you can send a calendar invite for 11:30am ET, we'll accept.

— Sara
Sara Jenkins
Head of ML Platform, Acme Corp
sara.jenkins@acme.com | (212) 555-0188

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC Kickoff - Recap & Next Steps

Sara — great questions, answers inline below and updated kickoff plan.

1) Latency target: 150ms p95 refers to warm-cache conditions (we will use a warm-up run at start of each window). We'll instrument both cold/warm in the runbook.

2) Logs & data isolation: For the POC we propose storing logs in Redwood-managed encrypted storage with daily exports to your GCP project via a secure transfer (we include export hooks in the runbook). If you prefer, we can also run the Dedicated instance inside your VPC (requires additional setup time; see timeline below).

3) MOU + data retention: I'll attach a one-page MOU summary in the DocuSign we send — it will include a 90-day default retention for audit logs with export & deletion options on request. Legal can redline; we expect this to be standard for a POC.

Updated proposed timeline:
- May 19: Kickoff meeting (30–45m) — confirm test accounts & owners
- May 20–21: Access & SSO setup (service account + SAML config)
- May 22–28: Model tuning, batching/caching config, run 1 of eval prompts
- May 29–Jun 2: Stabilization, performance runs, final evals & cost analysis
- Jun 3: POC wrap & success review (share results dashboard and next steps)

Owners & contacts:
- Marissa Cole (AE) — commercial, schedule, MOU
- Rishi Malhotra (Solutions Eng) — onboarding, runbook, perf tuning (rishi.malhotra@redwood.com)
- Vanessa Ortiz (Customer Success) — success criteria and rollout plan

I've attached the POC scope + sample prompt/eval file. I'll send the DocuSign link for the MOU once you confirm May 19.

Attaching: acme-poc-scope.xlsx, acme-sample-prompt-set.csv

Would you like the kickoff invite for 11:30am ET on Tue 19th? If so I'll send it now.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC Kickoff - Recap & Next Steps

Looping in a quick technical checklist so folks know what I'll need to start on day 1: 
- Service account email for API access + SAML SSO admin contact
- Sample production prompt & alternative prompts (we'll use the attached CSV)
- Baseline metrics: current p95 latency, average tokens per request, current spend per 1k tokens

Sara — if you can drop the service account and one sample request (anonymized) into the shared Drive folder, I can get the initial warm-up runs ready before kickoff.

Also recommending a 30m pre-kickoff alignment Monday morning (May 18) for the internal team only to coordinate the runbook — happy to do it if that help.

— Rishi
